t.6.3.1: Having heard the well-reasoned words of Sugrīva, Kākutstha, knower of the highest truth, accepted them and then spoke to Hanūmān.
t.6.3.2: Whether by sheer force, by building a bridge, or by drying up the ocean, I am in every way fully capable of crossing this sea.
t.6.3.3: Tell me how many fortifications the impregnable Laṅkā has. I wish to know all of it, O vānara, as though I were seeing it with my own eyes.
t.6.3.6: Having heard Rāma's words, Hanūmān, the son of Māruta, the foremost among those skilled in speech, then spoke these words to Rāma once again.
t.6.3.5: Tell me everything you have seen in Laṅkā, at your ease, exactly as it is and in truth, for you are skilled in every way.
t.6.3.4: The size of the army, the construction of the gates and fortifications, the defensive measures of Laṅkā, and the dwellings of the rākṣasas as well.
t.6.3.7: Let it be heard: I shall tell you everything, how the city of Laṅkā is made secure through the arrangement of its fortifications, and how it is guarded by troops.
t.6.3.9: Laṅkā is joyful and delighted, thronged with rutting elephants; the great city is filled with chariots and crowded with hosts of Rākṣasas.
t.6.3.8: The supreme prosperity of Laṅkā and the fearsomeness of the ocean, the division of the mass of troops and the disposition of the mounts.
t.6.3.10: Her four gates are wide and exceedingly great, fitted with firmly fastened doors and with massive iron bars.
t.6.3.11: On the ramparts are stone-hurling engines, powerful and huge, and by them an approaching enemy army is driven back there.
t.6.3.12: At the gates, hundreds of fearsome śataghnīs, made of black iron and sharpened, have been set in place and made ready by heroic bands of rākṣasas.
t.6.3.13: And her great golden rampart is hard to assail, its spaces inlaid with gems, coral, cat's-eye and pearls.
t.6.3.14: And on every side lie moats, exceedingly fearsome, with cool waters, very fine, fathomless, infested with crocodiles and frequented by fish.
t.6.3.15: At their gates there are four very long bridges, equipped with many large mechanical devices with strong joints.
t.6.3.16: There the bridges are guarded, and when an enemy army approaches, they are hurled down by those machines into the moats on every side.
t.6.3.17: But one bridge is unshakable, strong and exceedingly firm, adorned with many golden pillars and with platforms.
t.6.3.18: Rāvaṇa himself, O Rāma, is well endowed by nature and eager for battle; he is ever alert and vigilant in inspecting his forces.
t.6.3.19: The city of Laṅkā stands without any support, inaccessible even to the gods and fearsome. Its defence is fourfold: of rivers, of mountains, of forests, and of man-made works.
t.6.3.21: Built upon the summit of a mountain, that city Laṅkā is a fortress like the city of the gods; filled with horses and elephants, it is supremely difficult to conquer.
t.6.3.20: O Rāghava, it stands on the farther shore of the ocean, whose other shore lies far away. There is no path for ships here, and on every side there is nothing to guide the way.
t.6.3.22: Iron bars, śataghnīs, and engines of many kinds adorn Laṅkā, the city of the evil-minded Rāvaṇa.
t.6.3.23: Here ten thousand rākṣasas are stationed at the western gate; they bear spears in their hands, are hard to assail, and all fight with the points of their swords.
t.6.3.24: Here a myriad of rākṣasas is stationed at the southern gate, with an army of four divisions; there too the warriors are unsurpassed.
t.6.3.25: Here a million rākṣasas are stationed at the eastern gate, all of them bearing shields and swords and likewise skilled in every kind of weapon.
t.6.3.26: Here at the northern gate is stationed an arbuda of rākṣasas: chariot-warriors and horsemen, sons of noble families, highly honored.
t.6.3.27: A hundred hundred-thousand unassailable yātudhānas hold the central garrison, together with more than ten million rākṣasas.
t.6.3.28: Those bridges were broken by me, and the moats were filled in; the city of Laṅkā was burned, and its ramparts were thrown down.
t.6.3.29: By whatever means it may be, let us cross the ocean, the abode of Varuṇa; let the city of Laṅkā be regarded by the monkeys as already destroyed.
t.6.3.30: Aṅgada, Dvivida, Mainda, Jāmbavān, Panasa, Nala, and Nīla the commander too are here; what need have you of the rest of the army?
t.6.3.32: Thus, give the order at once for the assembling of all the forces, and resolve upon setting out at an auspicious hour.
t.6.3.31: Leaping across and reaching that great city of Rāvaṇa, with its ramparts and its mansions, they will surely bring back Maithilī.
